added.summary: A control element takes its inside from a control document: a component document that declares <meta name="control" content="progress"> (a tag with optional attribute tests, as input[type=range]) is instantiated under every element it names. Its props read the host's attributes, :host and :host(...) style the host under the rules written for it where it stands, and an element with part="name" is the host's ::part(name), which a pack's or a document's ::part() rule outranks. The cook bundles a control document when a game's documents have its element.

The engine's @ui/controls/progress.svelte and @ui/controls/meter.svelte draw <progress> and <meter>: track and fill are elements, reached as before through ::part(track) and ::part(fill). A game replaces one with its own control document for the element (og ui eject controls/progress).
A <meter> carries HTML's region of its value as its region attribute (optimum, suboptimum or poor) for its own document's selectors as well as its parts': meter[region=poor] { ... } matches.

A document holds UI state of its own: <meta name="state:open" content="bool"> (number, string or bool, with data-default) gives each instance of the document, and each host of a control document, its own value, read by its name and written with bind: (<details bind:open={open}>). A snapshot carries it, and it goes when the instance does. Use it for what the game has no stake in (a picker open, the tab shown); $state stays refused.

fixed.summary: revert-layer in a rule that reaches an element from another document (a ::part() rule on a control document's part) rolls back that document's layers only and then falls to the element's own document, instead of also discarding the element's own rules.

A separator is drawn by the default style's hr rule (a --stroke-hairline line in currentColor, --line by default; vertical stands it up) instead of by og-ui, so hr { color; block-size } and any other rule for hr restyle it as CSS does.
